Sean — thanks for the clear ask. High-level options below (summary + quick tradeoffs). I attached a pricing matrix (Pricing_Options_Table.xlsx) and a draft SOW (Greenline_SOW_v1.pdf) you can circulate.

Option A — Usage-floor + lower platform fee
- Structure: monthly committed tokens (usage floor) + platform fee at 6% of committed spend.
- Good for: unpredictable bursts where token usage matters more than steady operator headcount.
- Tradeoffs: requires committing to a minimum spend (we can tier the floor by site). Lower upfront ops commitment from you.

Option B — Operator-license (per-operator seat / per-node) + higher platform fee
- Structure: per-operator license + platform fee at 10% of run-rate. Operator licenses priced per seat; node-based bundles available for heavy inference hosts.
- Good for: customers who want predictable O&M responsibility and lower per-token pricing. Also useful if you expect steady sustained use and want to bundle SRE support.
- Tradeoffs: higher fixed fee exposure if you buy many seats; covers runbook handover and standard quarterly health-check in our Tier 2 support.

Support clarity:
- Standard Tier 1 (email + business hours) — included with both models.
- Tier 2 (SLA-backed, 24/7 paging, runbook creation, quarterly health-checks) — available as a support retainer or included when operator-license bundle is purchased at the Enterprise band.

Recommendation: For a multi-site, bursty 24/7 rollout, Option A with a staged usage floor (per site pilot floor that scales after month 3) preserves cost flexibility while you validate patterns. If Greenline prefers faster time-to-production handoff with our team owning runbook/oncall, Option B with operator licenses + Tier 2 retainer is cleaner.

I'll loop in our pricing lead to propose concessioning (credits, pilot discounts) and concrete numbers.

Regards,
